races.name: AJA Novice Flat Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes (For Riders With 3 Wins Or Fewer At Start Of Season)

runners_data.name: Made All
runners_data.note: Likely to find herself at the front by default in a field with no genuine pace, giving her a positional advantage in a sprint finish; five-year-old with good-ground form, trained by Sam England who has had one recent winner from four runners, returns after 48 days off carrying 159lbs which is the top weight.

runners_data.name: Cougar
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who holds soft-ground form from recent winning efforts but steps back onto good turf here — a natural hold-up horse whose true running style means a crowded midfield in a slow-run race is not where he'll thrive, tempering his prospects noticeably.

runners_data.name: Palazzo Persico
runners_data.note: Showed capability to win on soft ground in October and brings a recent run 24 days ago; Tony Carroll has been busy with 3 winners from 42 runners in the past fortnight, and this five-year-old's best turf form came over shorter, so the 1m4f trip and drop to good going are questions to answer.

runners_data.name: He's Our Cracker
runners_data.note: In-form trainer Jennie Candlish sends out this four-year-old fresh off a 19-day turnaround, but his recent form has been assembled on standard Tapeta surfaces rather than turf, and good ground is an unknown — he's a horse placed at the rear naturally but the race shape may force him further forward than ideal.

runners_data.name: Ruler Of The River
runners_data.note: Stays well — his last five runs have been over distances from 21f to 24f, making this 1m4f trip a significant drop in trip; pulled up most recently, and while he has winning form on good ground, the shorter distance and his natural hold-up style in a sprint-finish scenario present a tough ask.

runners_data.name: On The Bubble
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher in second and third on good ground, including a runner-up effort over 9f 15 days ago; races out of his natural hold-up position in this shape, but his good-ground speed figures are the most credible in the field and his sharp turn of foot could prove valuable if traffic clears.

races.paceDynamic: With every runner in this six-horse field carrying a hold-up profile, there is no confirmed front-runner to set a tempo over this mile-and-four-furlong trip at Catterick, meaning the race is almost certain to begin at a crawl before erupting into a sprint finish in the straight. Made All, despite her name suggesting otherwise, has run as a hold-up horse in recent starts, and none of Cougar, He's Our Cracker, Ruler Of The River, or On The Bubble have the natural speed or inclination to force the early pace. The likely outcome is a muddling gallop with the field bunched together until jockeys ask questions approaching the two-furlong marker, at which point positional luck and a sharp turn of foot over a short distance will determine the outcome. This race shape strongly favours horses with proven finishing speed and the ability to find a clear run in a slowly-run sprint — those who have shown tactical versatility and can produce a quick, sustained effort over the final two furlongs. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the back in a compact six-runner field; Cougar, He's Our Cracker, Ruler Of The River, and On The Bubble are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield slots, with Made All and Palazzo Persico the most likely to secure a forward position by default given the absence of genuine pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish From Front
scenarios.trigger: If no horse forces the pace and the field drifts into a slow-run sprint, the horses nearest the front at the two-furlong pole gain a decisive positional edge.
scenarios.body: With no true pace-setter, whoever gravitates to the front in the first mile faces no serious challenge and can conserve energy before kicking late; Made All and Palazzo Persico, likely to be forward by default, are best placed to exploit this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Lands Late Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is marginally stronger than expected and those up front are caught out in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A slightly quicker early gallop stretches the field fractionally, giving a horse with genuine late pace the room to weave through and pounce close home; On The Bubble has the best recent evidence of finishing strongly on good ground and is the likeliest beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches dangerously tight, creating a messy finish in which a lower-rated runner finds daylight at the crucial moment.
scenarios.body: A small, compact field at a crawl can produce traffic issues for fancied rivals, leaving a horse like Ruler Of The River — who has shown course-and-distance aptitude over staying trips — to emerge with a clear run at the right moment.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Edge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If jockeys misjudge the pace, allowing a strong gallop to develop mid-race that tests the field's stamina over the full mile and four furlongs.
scenarios.body: A genuine test of staying power would expose runners who lack the required distance credentials, lifting horses like Ruler Of The River — with experience over longer trips — above the sprint specialists.

watchPoints.text: Watch Made All and Palazzo Persico drifting to the front unchallenged in the opening half-mile — whoever leads by default controls the tempo and could prove very hard to pass in a sprint finish.

Ruler Of The River is racing over a trip far shorter than his recent assignments; monitor whether his jockey Mr Jack Loughnane attempts to recreate a stamina-based contest by pushing on early, as this could transform the entire pace dynamic.

On The Bubble carries a STYLE_FIT concern after being redistributed from his natural hold-up position; watch for traffic trouble if the field bunches in the final two furlongs, as a clear run is critical to his finishing effort.

Top weight Made All carries 159lbs — in a race that ends in a sprint, monitor whether the weight burden affects her acceleration in the final furlong compared to the lighter-framed On The Bubble (140lbs) and Ruler Of The River (140lbs).

Cougar's two most recent wins both came on soft ground; if the going description remains unknown and dries out further toward good-to-firm on the day, his chance diminishes further given his soft-ground dependence in form.

races.name: EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Lion Of Persia
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner by style but form figures of 8-4 show progressive improvement; Robert Cowell has a live 1/8 14-day record and Marco Ghiani rides, with good-going form confirmed across two runs — well-placed if he travels close enough on the steady tempo.

runners_data.name: Longshanks Luke
runners_data.note: Debut runner with no public form to assess; Patrick Neville yard is lightly represented (0/5 over 14 days) and going preference is entirely unknown — an unknown quantity who could emerge or disappear without warning.

runners_data.name: Neverbeatdeswalker
runners_data.note: Sole run was a moderate seventh over six furlongs on good, stepping down to five today which is an unknown; Mark Walford's yard is out of recent form (0/13) and the 32-day gap adds uncertainty to a horse with very little exposed ability.

runners_data.name: Johns Power
runners_data.note: Form figures of 0-6 offer little encouragement; a natural hold-up runner pushed into a midfield slot by the congestion of rear-pacers, meaning Joanna Mason will need to override the horse's instincts to get any meaningful position — style fit discounted.

runners_data.name: Kaiulani Spirit
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's yard is in strong form (6/70) and this horse has placed at 5f on good ground; however its natural preference to settle toward the rear sits awkwardly in a race with a gentle pace and no speed to chase, with Duran Fentiman carrying the burden of overcoming that structural disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Mick's The Boy
runners_data.note: The race's lone pace-setter and key shape-setter; form of 2-8 shows one placed effort at 6f on good, steps back to 5f today, and Lewis Chalkley (7lb claimer) takes the ride — as the controlling influence, the tactical outcome of this race flows from how well he manages the fractions.

runners_data.name: Mr De Maggs
runners_data.note: Sole run was a distant tenth at 6f on good, and a fade-in-finish flag compounds the concern on an uphill Catterick finish; Tony Culhane & Stella Barclay are small operators (1/4) and there is nothing in the profile to suggest competitiveness here.

runners_data.name: South West
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope is a major positive and the horse has placed figures including a third at 6f good; OR of 67 is conspicuously lower than the OR=120 field but blinkers are applied and the yard (Richard Hughes, 4/34) is in fair nick — true hold-up style means Tudhope must manufacture a position that isn't natural to the horse.

runners_data.name: Prosperity Angel
runners_data.note: Debut runner like Longshanks Luke, carrying zero public form into this race; Andrew Mullen rides for Ben Haslam (0/7 over 14 days) and going preference is entirely unknown — treat as a complete wildcard with upside only on raw ability.

runners_data.name: Cheeky Chesca
runners_data.note: Consistent form figures including multiple placed efforts suggest she gets into races; fitted with a hood and Tim Easterby's yard is firing (6/70), but her natural home toward the rear of the field is a recurring problem when a lazy pace is set — David Allan will need to ride positively against her instincts.

races.paceDynamic: Mick's The Boy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner novice sprint and should bowl along at a controlled, solo gallop from the outset — with no rival equipped or motivated to chase him hard, this is a genuinely uncontested lead scenario over five furlongs at Catterick. The pace is therefore sustainable rather than scorching, which typically compresses the finish and rewards horses that travel close to the speed rather than those making up ground late. This field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate: Kaiulani Spirit, Johns Power, South West and Cheeky Chesca are all natural rear-runners redistributed to a midfield position on the map, but only the most tractable or jockey-overridden of them will genuinely travel there — most will settle where horses naturally settle when given a soft gallop, which is behind the pace and facing an uphill task over a short trip. The race shape favours prominent and close-tracking runners who can latch onto Mick's The Boy's rhythm and pounce in the final furlong, with deep closers at a structural disadvantage on a flat five-furlong track with a steady tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mick's Boy Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Mick's The Boy dictates a controlled tempo unchallenged and the field settles in a compact group behind.
scenarios.body: Mick's The Boy bowls along at his own pace and the compact chasing group struggles to find gears late, leaving the lead rider to kick clear or hold on through the final furlong; prominent trackers who latch onto the leader early are best placed to capitalise if he ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a close-tracking runner travels smoothly just off the pace and delivers a well-timed challenge inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The steady tempo means little fuel is burned early and a horse settled in second or third can produce a sustained effort to collar Mick's The Boy near the line; this shape suits any runner who can naturally race in the first three without being bustled along.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Cut Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply mid-race and the front half tightens, opening a gap for a finishing run.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected gallop would compress the front group and allow hold-up horses to find daylight, but this is structurally unlikely given one relaxed pace-setter and a 5f trip that limits recovery time; South West and Kaiulani Spirit would be the nominal beneficiaries, though both are racing out of their natural rear-of-field position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Mick's The Boy misses the break or checks sharply, creating a scrambled pace scenario with no true leader.
scenarios.body: Without a settled gallop the race devolves into a messy sprint from the gates and an unexposed or lightly raced runner could bolt in on raw ability; Longshanks Luke and Prosperity Angel, both unknown quantities on debut, are the wildcards here.

watchPoints.text: Mick's The Boy controls every tactical variable in this race — if he misses the start or is forced wide, the entire race shape collapses and the probabilities reset entirely.

Kaiulani Spirit, Johns Power, South West and Cheeky Chesca are all natural hold-up horses and if they flood the rear of the field simultaneously, the midfield could become chaotic and none of them will be in a position to win.

Lion Of Persia steps up in class but Robert Cowell's 1/8 14-day strike rate is a genuine positive signal — watch how close Marco Ghiani positions him in the early furlongs as a guide to whether he can feature.

Longshanks Luke and Prosperity Angel are both debutants with unknown profiles — either could bolt up or fail to handle the track; their odds movements and paddock demeanour are the only pre-race evidence available.

The going report is listed as unknown across all Catterick markers — if the surface rides faster or slower than standard good, horses with soft-ground or firm-ground form exclusively should be reassessed accordingly.

races.name: racingtv.com/freetrial Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lady Dublin
runners_data.note: Unclassified style makes her the de facto pace-setter in this no-front-runner field; Ollie Pears has a cold 0/4 over 14 days and the step back to 6f from recent 7f run looks sensible, with two placed efforts on similar good ground underpinning her going credentials — headgear (p) noted

runners_data.name: Mardy Bum
runners_data.note: David O'Meara fires with 2/51 in the past fortnight and this hold-up horse was a placed third over 5f on good ground last time, suggesting form is live; the step up to 6f is a key question mark having run short of a mile so far, but Mark Winn is a capable handler of this type

runners_data.name: Sunrise At Dawn
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose form figures of 586 tell a difficult story — she has not placed in three starts and has not run beyond 6f, finding good ground on each occasion without threatening; a third-career outing and a fresh 30-day break leave her needing significant improvement to factor here

runners_data.name: Showmethebubbles
runners_data.note: Ellison has recent form (2/12) that keeps her relevant despite 50 days off, but this horse's natural style is hold-up and she has been mapped to midfield purely because the field cannot accommodate three genuine closers at the rear — her 855 form figures and a [STYLE_FIT=0.90] flag caution strongly against overstating her chance if she fails to find a position that suits

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this four-runner field, none of Lady Dublin, Mardy Bum, Sunrise At Dawn, or Showmethebubbles has a natural inclination to boss the pace from the front, meaning the early gallop is likely to be modest and the race will compress into a sprint finish over the final two furlongs. Lady Dublin is the only runner with an unclassified style (U), making her the most likely candidate to take a forward position by default, but she has shown no strong front-running tendencies in recent form. Mardy Bum and Sunrise At Dawn are genuine hold-up types who will settle in behind and look for a late run, and Showmethebubbles — though mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear — is also a true hold-up horse whose redistribution to a middle position is a mapping necessity, not a reflection of her racing pattern. This race shape, given the lack of genuine pace, most strongly favours a horse capable of travelling prominently without forcing the issue and then quickening in a slowly-run sprint — making Lady Dublin's positional flexibility the most relevant tactical factor.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow pace, sprint finish
scenarios.trigger: If no runner commits to the front and the field drifts into a crawl before a furious final-furlong dash
scenarios.body: Lady Dublin, unable to be dominated from the front, drifts into a handy position and benefits most from a sprint, while runners from the rear struggle to generate enough momentum from a standing start

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lady Dublin controls tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Dublin takes the initiative from the front end and sets a measured, controlled gallop that suits her stamina
scenarios.body: Dictating at a steady pace on good ground which matches her recent going form, she gives nothing away to the hold-up trio who lack the acceleration in a strongly-run finish

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers pounce late
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Dublin or another runner sets a strong enough gallop for Mardy Bum or Sunrise At Dawn to produce a sustained run
scenarios.body: Mardy Bum brings recent course-and-distance experience and a trainer in David O'Meara with a live 2/51 fortnight strike rate, giving this hold-up type legitimate claims if pace materialises; however, Showmethebubbles — the third hold-up type here — is not a genuine closer in disguise and her redistribution to midfield should temper expectations

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete upset, outsider wins
scenarios.trigger: If Showmethebubbles bounces back after 50 days off and finds an uncontested position to stalk from midfield
scenarios.body: Brian Ellison has 2/12 in the last 14 days and this drop to OR 50 could mark a competitive opportunity on return, but the extended layoff, poor recent form figures of 855, and out-of-role positional challenge make this a genuinely low-probability shape

watchPoints.text: Lady Dublin's willingness to go forward — if she shows even minimal pace-making instinct from stall, she controls the tempo of this race and makes the shape entirely predictable
Mardy Bum's trip — six furlongs is unproven for this hold-up horse and if the sprint materialises late, his stamina question could be exposed just as he comes alive

Showmethebubbles returning from 50 days off — horses returning after seven-plus weeks with flat 2-year-old form of 855 on soft going into good ground at a track change are a flag for drifting rather than improving

Watch the early strides for any horse attempting to go forward — in a field of four with no confirmed leader, whoever takes the initiative in the first furlong effectively dictates the entire race shape

races.name: Try Racing Tv For Free Now Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mudamer
runners_data.note: Carries top weight of 137lbs off an OR of 81 and has finished placed at this trip on good going multiple times, but his trainer has a poor recent record (0/3 in 14 days) and his true style is prominent — he is shown at the rear only because the field has no natural hold-up runners to fill that slot, so expect him to be closer to the pace than his map position suggests.

runners_data.name: Haaderr
runners_data.note: The standout pace angle here — three runs all finished first or second with winning form at this trip on soft/standard going, now returning after 281 days off for Bethell's yard which has been in strong form (11/32 in 14 days); Tudhope takes the ride and should be able to dictate from the front in a field that offers no genuine challenge for the lead.

runners_data.name: Naval Light
runners_data.note: Stepped up to win over 6f on soft last time out and has solid each-way form at 7f on good ground, making the trip switch look straightforward; Burke's operation is ticking along (7/44) and the 5lb claimer Jack Nicholls keeps the burden to 131lbs, giving him a competitive profile as the most likely horse to press Haaderr late.

runners_data.name: Woodstock
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a modest OR of 74 and recent form of 6-7346, carrying headgear (visors) that Ruth Carr has used to try to sharpen her; she is a genuine prominent racer by nature but the congested front end means she is likely to find herself further back than ideal, and her 12/15 similar-going record hides a consistent absence of winners.

races.paceDynamic: Haaderr is the confirmed front-runner here and, in a field of just four where every other runner is a prominent type, he is almost certain to lead unchallenged from the outset over Catterick's seven furlongs. Naval Light, Mudamer, and Woodstock are all naturally prominent racers, meaning none are true pressers from off the pace, and Haaderr can dictate a controlled, honest gallop without being harassed into overdoing it. This field holds more prominent types than the shape can accommodate — Woodstock and Mudamer are the most likely to concede their natural position, tracking a length or two off Haaderr's shoulder rather than sitting alongside him. With a single uncontested leader setting a sustainable pace in a small field, horses who can sit just off the fractions and quicken in the straight are best placed — the race shape most favours a prominent racer with tactical speed and the ability to collar a relaxed front-runner inside the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Haaderr Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Haaderr trots into a soft lead and dictates a rhythm that suits him, allowing him to quicken off his own pace in the straight.
scenarios.body: Haaderr has winning form at this trip on good ground and arrives fresh after 281 days off, with Tudhope giving him an uncontested rail and a chance to show his class from the front; the small field means no one is able to disrupt his rhythm.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Haaderr over-relaxes and sets too slow a pace, allowing a tight-tracking prominent horse to collar him on the Catterick rise.
scenarios.body: Naval Light has placed at 7f on good ground multiple times and travels prominently with enough tactical speed to exploit a soft lead; Burke's yard have been placing horses well recently and the 5lb claimer keeps the weight down.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Woodstock Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and Woodstock, dropped back out of her natural position, produces a late run from the rear of the small group.
scenarios.body: Woodstock has modest recent form and an OR of 74, making this a tough ask, but Ruth Carr's runner does have placed form at 7f on good ground and visors have been tried previously to sharpen her up; this scenario depends on her racing out of her true role, which limits its likelihood.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Tactical Race
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so modest that the race degenerates into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole, flattening the hierarchy.
scenarios.body: Mudamer, the oldest runner at seven and carrying 137lbs, has enough positional flexibility to slot into a race that becomes a flat-out dash, though his recent form figures of 7-3306 give limited confidence; this scenario is the least likely given the clear pace picture.

watchPoints.text: Haaderr sets fractions so slow that a 281-day absence leaves him short of a full gallop, handing Naval Light a simple task to pick him off in the final furlong.
Woodstock and Mudamer both competing for the same prominent position behind Haaderr could create a bunched, slow-tempo contest that scrambles the form book.
Mudamer's 137lb burden is the heaviest in the race and could become decisive if the pace quickens sharply in the final two furlongs on the Catterick rise.

Naval Light is the only runner to have won last time out and steps up in trip — monitor early market moves as any confidence from the Burke yard could compress his price significantly in a four-runner heat.

races.name: Racing Again 22nd July Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: South Shore
runners_data.note: Progressive form with back-to-back wins including a 5f good-ground success 9 days ago; Marco Ghiani retains the ride for Robert Cowell who is 1/8 over 14 days — sharp, prominent racer ideally placed to exploit this race shape at a course where she handles the going well.

runners_data.name: Our Absent Friends
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who sets the entire pace dynamic, but a Form string of 206379 and just 2 days since last run raises questions about freshness and merit — five of the last five on good or similar going returned just one placed finish; Jason Hart will need to judge the fractions precisely.

runners_data.name: Invincible Crown
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's four-year-old is the most credible hold-up threat with a genuine closing style and a win plus two places from seven good-ground 5f starts; James Sullivan is an experienced handler of this type and 15 days between runs looks ideal — pure closer who needs the pace to hold a fraction longer.

runners_data.name: Albegone
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's veteran sprinter carries blinkers and genuine hold-up inclinations, but with six Tim Easterby runners over 14 days and a 23-day break, its true racing style sits at the rear despite being mapped to midfield due to field congestion — David Allan will struggle to place him naturally if the pace is moderate.

runners_data.name: Edmond Halley
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in finishes, and a form string of 50-007 with an 81-day absence are significant concerns; Cian Horgan takes a 5lb claim but the Bethell yard is 11/32 over 14 days suggesting activity without consistent results — this horse's profile does not suit a controlled-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Lucius Aurelius
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's four-year-old wears a hood and scored at 5f on good ground, making him interesting if the pace is brisk enough to bring hold-up horses into play; Jack Nicholls claims 5lb and with 16 days between runs the horse arrives in reasonable order — one win from six on good or softer suggests a reliable but not dominant type.

runners_data.name: Irish Dancer
runners_data.note: Two wins from eight on good going and a hat-trick of placed efforts in comparable conditions make Irish Dancer one of the most reliable prominent types in the race; Zak Wheatley takes the ride for Declan Carroll whose yard is 1/7 over 14 days, and the tongue-tie plus breast-girth combination suggests the stable is fine-tuning for peak effort.

runners_data.name: Zuffolo
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' blinkered six-year-old is a genuine hold-up runner whose best form (second at 5f on good) comes when the pace forces the field back to him — mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear, his true position will be further back than the map shows, making Rhys Elliott's task harder in a race unlikely to suit.

runners_data.name: Gwen Tennyson
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's three-year-old has placed in recent 5f good-ground races but is a natural hold-up type carried forward on the map by field redistribution; Connor Beasley is an experienced rider and 15 days since last run is acceptable, but with a style-fit score of 0.90 the most likely scenario is that she struggles to get competitive unless the race falls apart.

races.paceDynamic: Our Absent Friends is the lone confirmed front-runner here, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, they should be able to stride into an uncontested position from the gates and control the tempo at a sustainable, measured clip over this 5f on good turf at Catterick. South Shore and Irish Dancer are the natural prominent racers most likely to track closely in second and third, giving the race a clean, predictable shape from flag to finish — the front two furlongs will be honest but not frenetic, which suits a horse who can coast in front. The hold-up brigade — Invincible Crown, Albegone, Lucius Aurelius, Edmond Halley, Zuffolo, and Gwen Tennyson — will be under pressure to close from off the pace on a track where Catterick's short 5f finish can catch pure closers out if the leader idles rather than ties up. This field carries more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate: Albegone, Zuffolo, and Gwen Tennyson are redistributed to midfield on the map, but South Shore and Irish Dancer are the horses most likely to actually secure the genuine prominent positions behind the leader. The race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can slot in immediately behind a controlled pace — horses that can travel within striking range and pick up without needing a gap to open late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Our Absent Friends dictates a comfortable, unforced pace and the prominent horses cannot sustain pressure late.
scenarios.body: Our Absent Friends leads without challenge, South Shore and Irish Dancer shadow in second and third but lack the finishing kick to reel in a horse who has conserved energy throughout; the front end dominates a race where the pace is never truly honest enough to stop the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Our Absent Friends fades inside the final furlong and one of the prominent stalkers accelerates sharply off the pace-setter's shoulder.
scenarios.body: South Shore, who has won twice at 5f on good ground recently, or Irish Dancer, with two wins on comparable going and strong course form at sprint trips, would be ideally placed to collar a tiring leader with a well-timed challenge; both have the form figures on this surface to justify being trusted in this position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Closes
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is faster than anticipated and opens ground for a horse finishing from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Invincible Crown, a genuine hold-up type with three placed efforts and a win at 5f on good at Catterick recently, represents the most credible threat from the rear; Lucius Aurelius, fitted with a hood and carrying course form, could also get involved if gaps materialise inside the final furlong, though Albegone and Zuffolo are racing partly out of role and their style fit is reduced.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If Our Absent Friends fails to find their stride and the race lacks any coherent pace, producing a muddled outcome.
scenarios.body: A slow, uneven tempo with runners bunching in the straight would favour a quick-accelerating type who can find a line, potentially allowing Gwen Tennyson or Zuffolo to benefit from chaos rather than genuine pace; both are true hold-up types racing partly out of role, so this scenario depends on circumstances beyond their tactical execution.

watchPoints.text: South Shore is on a short 9-day turnaround following a win and Marco Ghiani retains the ride — watch for any market drift that suggests a negative vet report or a track bias against prominent runners developing in earlier races.

Our Absent Friends ran just 2 days ago, and while confirmed as the pace-setter, a tired front-runner who idles in front can create a falsely slow tempo that compresses the field — watch how freely they travel in the opening two furlongs.

Albegone, Zuffolo, and Gwen Tennyson are all genuine hold-up types competing for the same back-of-field position — if the pace is moderate, three horses trying to close from the same place increases the chance of traffic issues and blocked runs in the final furlong at Catterick.

Edmond Halley's 81-day absence combined with a fade-in-finish flag is a combination to monitor in the market — significant late shortening would be unusual and worth noting, but drift would confirm the layoff concern is priced in by the market.
